doc.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

chapter: Personal life and the future of jazz
title: Young song players: Harry Allen, Scott Hamilton and Ruby Braff's influence
summary: Moore praises Harry Allen, Scott Hamilton and Ken Peplowski as song players and traces the line back to Ruby Braff.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well, that’s positive. I’m glad to hear that. You’ve worked with, gee, about the greatest in the business, and the list keeps coming. And I’m really glad to see some of the younger players coming, Harry Allen and those guys, embracing this kind of music and keeping it alive.

Harry told me that Johnny Mandel heard his record, called him on the phone, he didn’t know him, called him on the phone and left a message on his answering machine saying he’d heard his CD and said how he was much relieved to know that jazz was in the hands of young players like him and how good it made him feel, which was a great day for Harry. But it’s true. I mean you think that — I remember when Scott Hamilton came around for the first time. And nobody remembers particularly what was going on, now, at the time. But Scott was a real pioneer in a way, because it wasn’t that he hadn’t heard John Coltrane or Ornette or all the people we were talking about before. He’d heard all that, but he liked playing songs, and he liked playing, and everybody was like wow.

What a concept, you know, and here’s this young guy doing it. He was in his twenties when I met him and he was playing like that. And I really think a lot of it is connected to Ruby Braff. Because Ruby went around bebop in a way. He’s not really bebop. He was a song player, but a modern song player. Even though Louis Armstrong and Hackett, those were his influences. But Ruby harmonically and everything is very advanced and very understanding. But his songs, and I think he was a hero to a lot of these younger guys that came along. And Ruby kind of, like through that whole period, stuck to his gun, played great songs and never went the other route at all. And I think that’s kind of the thread that runs then into Scott, and Harry is the next generation. Harry loved Scott. And we just did a tour in England with the two of them playing together, it was great. They both sounded wonderful. It was a pretty nice experience. So it is true there are young players out there that come along that have kind of digested the whole thing. Ken Peplowski is another one. I mean he probably has a better record collection, and is more eclectic than I have ever been as far as what he listens to and everything else. But he knows how he wants to play and what he loves is those songs, and carrying on that tradition.
